verification_legend.VERIFIED: Value appears verbatim in an official source retrieved in this session; the source URL is in the row.
verification_legend.DERIVED: Value is arithmetic on two or more VERIFIED values. The formula is shown in `note`. Not a substitute for a primary figure.
verification_legend.FLAGGED: A value or a claim was located but the source is secondary, paywalled, internally inconsistent, or could not be read directly. Where even the number could not be read, the value cell is left BLANK and only the qualitative finding is published.
verification_legend.UNVERIFIED: No official source could confirm the value. The value cell is intentionally BLANK. Nothing has been inferred or estimated.

categories.title: Tenant Credit — Jack in the Box Inc.
categories.blurb: Every figure below is from Jack in the Box Inc.'s FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the SEC. This is the franchise system's health, not necessarily the health of the specific operating franchisee.

rows.note: "As of September 28, 2025, Jack in the Box operated and franchised 2,136 quick-service restaurants."

rows.metric: Franchised share of Jack in the Box system
rows.note: 1,986 of 2,136, or 93%, were franchised. Only 150 company-operated.

rows.metric: Jack in the Box restaurants in California
rows.note: California is the largest single state for the brand: 96 company-operated + 845 franchised = 941. Texas is second at 549.
"...an initial franchise fee of $50,000 per restaurant for a 20-year term, and royalty and marketing payments generally set at 5.0% of gross sales."
Some legacy agreements are higher; some newer are lower for a limited time. Actual FY2025 realized royalty rate was 5.1% of franchised sales.

rows.note: Down from $1,949K in FY2024 (-3.9%). A $1.874M unit at a 5% royalty yields ~$94K/yr of franchisor royalty.

rows.note: (1,874 - 1,949) / 1,949. Both endpoints VERIFIED.
Franchise -4.3%; company -3.7%. FY2024 was -1.3%. Two consecutive negative years is a material credit signal.
Traffic fell 5.7% and was only partly offset by +2.0% average check. The decline is a guest-count problem, not a pricing problem.
Pricing power is being outrun by traffic loss — a classic value-segment squeeze.
